subject: calderMobile
pitch:
Category: Abstract.
Subject: hanging mobile.
Style: Alexander Calder.

requests.what: Thin white painted rim line and a tiny rivet-like pivot dot where the wire joins the big red disc, in WHITE and BLACK.
Slim raised midrib and a few short side veins on the blue leaf in a darker BLUE_DARK, as thin strips seated on its face.
Two small round cut-out-look dots in BLACK and a thin BLACK edge line near the tip of the long yellow leaf.
A row of three small WHITE dots along the flat top edge of the black half-disc.
A tiny YELLOW disc inset in the small red disc, as a layered bullseye.
Small black counterweight beads and twisted wire loops at the ends of the top arm.
Brass-like hook and swivel detail under the ceiling canopy, with a small collar ring.
A small WHITE ellipse accent hung on a short extra wire from the middle of the second arm.
Subtle brushed matte paint in RED with faint darker brush strokes and a few tiny chips showing grey metal.
Matte BLUE paint with slight sprayed gradient toward the tip and fine edge wear.
Sunny YELLOW enamel with soft hand-painted streaks along its length.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing a hanging Calder mobile, planning for it to hang from a ceiling hook near the top with the lowest element positioned just above the ground, keeping the overall composition rich but efficient.

Since the mobile is static, I'll skip joints and build the structure directly from rods and parts, using a wire helper to connect hook points to arms and arms to elements. I'm sketching the layout of a balanced tree of crossbars at varying heights, with wires branching down to discs and sub-arms positioned asymmetrically to keep the composition feeling balanced.

Now I'm defining the shapes that will hang from the mobile — discs, leaves, drops, crescents — as flat extruded outlines generated from simple point functions like ellipse and leaf, oriented so their top point aligns with the wire attachment.

Now I'm designing the recursive hierarchy for the mobile: each arm hangs from a wire attach point, splits into two ends via a yaw angle, and children (arms or elements) recursively attach at those ends, so a `place` function walks the tree computing hang points and drawing wires and rods accordingly.

Working out the actual depth values for a sample tree, assigning drop lengths, wire lengths, and element sizes so the structure balances downward from y≈2.3 toward the floor, mixing discs and leaf shapes at different levels.

I still need to add a hook ring at the very top, probably using a torus geometry around y≈2.8.

Now I'm settling on the Calder color palette—red, blue, yellow, black, white, with near-black wire—and planning seven total additions with three textured surfaces, giving each shape element a clear name for texture reference.

I'm computing the actual arm endpoint coordinates by working through the direction vectors and yaw angles, defining endA and endB relative to the hub position so the red disc and leaf shapes land at the correct x/z offsets.

Still working out tree geometry...

Continuing with arm4's geometry, I work out endA and the red disc's position, landing on a request point around (-1.26, 1.2, -0.06) with a normal facing forward. I note the extrude approach for the outline shapes, placing origins at the top and centering the disc ellipse appropriately.

For the semi-circle outline I trace points along the bottom arc using angle sweeps so the flat edge sits at the top, letting it hang naturally from the center point rather than needing a triangle shape. I add thin wire rods for structure, small white and black accent discs for the tips, and work out the hook assembly with a ring torus and canopy cylinder stacked near the top, bringing the total height to about 2.97.

I'm working out how to add veins to the blue leaf, locating its mesh in the scene graph and calculating the outline geometry based on its rotation and dimensions so the veins align correctly with the leaf shape.

Still building vein geometry...

I realize the requested coordinates might not match the actual rendered positions, so I should instead locate the real meshes by traversing the scene for names like "yellowLeaf" and compute their actual bounding boxes before placing details.

From there, I'm working out the geometry: computing each leaf's front face normal from its rotation angle, then planning to place small half-disc shapes aligned to that normal on both sides of the leaf surface so they're visible from either viewing angle, offset slightly to avoid z-fighting with the mesh.

Still placing rod segments...

I'm computing the pivot as the bbox center with max height, then mapping local leaf-space coordinates (direction and vertical offset, plus a normal offset for thickness) into world points for both faces, including small white dots near the leaf base.
